evidence_items.name: Rental / Lease Agreement
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves the contractual tenancy terms and the exact security deposit amount agreed upon.

evidence_items.name: Deposit Payment Proof / Bank Transfer Receipt
evidence_items.why_needed: Establishes that the security deposit money was actually paid into the landlord's account.

evidence_items.name: Move-out Photographs / Video Proof
evidence_items.why_needed: Rebuts false damage claims or excessive painting deductions made by the landlord.

evidence_items.name: WhatsApp / Email Communications
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves you gave timely notice to vacate and requested the deposit peacefully.

stages.title: Deposit Requested Informally
stages.description: Tenant vacated premises and requested deposit refund via phone, chat, or email.

stages.title: Formal Written Notice Issued
stages.description: A written demand records the facts, the requested refund, and a reasonable response date chosen for this case.

stages.title: Awaiting Landlord Response
stages.description: Notice served; waiting for landlord to refund or state formal objections.

stages.title: Rent Authority / Civil Recovery Petition
stages.description: Consider the appropriate State rent authority or civil recovery forum after checking local law, jurisdiction, and the agreement.

rights_summary.what_this_means: Your right to a deposit refund usually depends on the tenancy agreement and the law in the State where the property is located. A landlord should be asked to explain and support any deduction.
possible_rights: Possible right to recover the balance deposit after lawful, documented deductions.
Possible contractual claim if the landlord breaches the refund terms in the tenancy agreement.
The correct forum and any interest claim depend on the applicable State law and contract.
useful_evidence: Copy of bank statement showing initial transfer
Condition photos on the date of vacating
rights_summary.legal_source: Tenancy agreement, applicable State tenancy/rent law, and potentially Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. The Model Tenancy Act is not automatically the governing law in every State.

evidence_items.name: Offer Letter / Employment Contract
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves the employment relationship, designated salary, and notice period obligations.

evidence_items.name: Past Salary Slips / Bank Credit Statements
evidence_items.why_needed: Demonstrates regular past compensation and established monthly wage rate.

evidence_items.name: Written Follow-up with HR / Management
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves you formally demanded payment of arrears and gave the employer opportunities to pay.

evidence_items.name: Resignation / Relieving Communication (if applicable)
evidence_items.why_needed: Establishes last working day and settlement timeline.

stages.title: Internal HR / Management Follow-up
stages.description: Employee followed up via internal emails or tickets regarding delayed compensation.

stages.title: Written Salary Demand Sent
stages.description: A factual salary demand is sent to HR or management with supporting employment records.

stages.title: Awaiting Employer Settlement
stages.description: Waiting for the response period stated in the written demand before reassessing escalation options.

stages.title: Labour Authority / Recovery Route
stages.description: The appropriate labour authority, contractual remedy, or court depends on the role, establishment, State, and current law.

rights_summary.what_this_means: Earned salary is normally payable under the employment terms and applicable wage or labour law. The correct authority depends on your role, establishment, State, and employment status.
possible_rights: Possible right to recover salary already earned under the employment contract and applicable wage law.
Possible grievance before a labour authority where the law covers the employee and establishment.
A civil or contractual remedy may be relevant in some cases; the correct route should be verified.
useful_evidence: Official work email threads acknowledging work done
Past 3 months salary credit bank statements
rights_summary.legal_source: Employment terms and applicable Central/State wage and labour law. Coverage and the competent authority must be verified for the employee and establishment.

evidence_items.name: Tax Invoice / Purchase Order Receipt
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves date of purchase, warranty coverage, and exact consideration paid.

evidence_items.name: Defect Photographs / Technician Job Sheet
evidence_items.why_needed: Conclusive evidence demonstrating the product failure or deficiency of service.

evidence_items.name: Customer Care Grievance History / Ticket IDs
evidence_items.why_needed: Establishes repeated failed attempts to seek replacement or service from the seller.

evidence_items.name: Seller / Platform Written Rejection Email
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves refusal to honor warranty, establishing cause of action for formal complaint.

stages.title: Customer Support Contacted
stages.description: Consumer raised return or repair request on portal or customer helpline.

stages.title: Formal Consumer Grievance Sent
stages.description: A written grievance records the defect, prior requests, evidence, and the remedy requested under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

stages.title: Awaiting Seller / Platform Response
stages.description: Waiting through the response period stated in the grievance before deciding whether to escalate.

stages.title: e-Daakhil Consumer Commission Complaint
stages.description: Formal complaint filed before District Consumer Commission under Section 35 CPA 2019.

rights_summary.what_this_means: A defective product or deficient service may support remedies under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The available remedy depends on the evidence, contract, warranty, and facts.
possible_rights: Possible repair, replacement, refund, or other relief if defect or deficiency is established.
Possible compensation where legally supported by the evidence and loss proved.
Possible online consumer-commission complaint after confirming territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction.
useful_evidence: Photographs / video of unboxing or defect

evidence_items.name: UPI / Net Banking Transaction Slip (UTR / Ref No)
evidence_items.why_needed: Contains critical 12-digit UTR/RRN number required by banks to track beneficiary accounts.

evidence_items.name: Chat Screenshots / Call Records with Fraudster
evidence_items.why_needed: Demonstrates deception, fake links, or phishing inducement.

evidence_items.name: Bank Fraud Reporting Acknowledgement
evidence_items.why_needed: Records when the bank was notified, which is relevant to the bank's investigation and any customer-liability assessment.

stages.title: Fraudulent Debit / Transfer Occurred
stages.description: Unauthorized transfer or scam transaction executed via UPI / Net Banking.

stages.title: Bank Alerted & 1930 Helpline Called
stages.description: The bank and Cyber Helpline 1930 are alerted promptly so they can consider available tracing or hold measures.

stages.title: Formal Cyber Crime Portal & Bank Requisition Drafted
stages.description: Complaint filed on cybercrime.gov.in and formal letter sent to Nodal Officer.

stages.title: Cyber Cell Police Complaint / FIR
stages.description: Escalation to the cybercrime police unit; the applicable offence provisions depend on how the fraud occurred.

rights_summary.what_this_means: Prompt reporting to the bank and the National Cyber Crime Reporting system can improve the chance of tracing funds. RBI customer-liability protection depends on whether the transaction was unauthorised and on the facts of the breach and reporting delay.
possible_rights: Possible zero or limited liability in the circumstances defined by the RBI framework for unauthorised electronic transactions.
Right to report the transaction promptly to the bank and request urgent tracing or hold measures.
Ability to report financial cyber fraud through 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.
useful_evidence: Bank statement showing debit with exact timestamp
Fraudster phone number, website link, or UPI ID
rights_summary.legal_source: RBI framework for unauthorised electronic banking transactions, the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, and offence provisions applicable to the facts.

CYBER_FRAUD.default_doc_label: Prepare Cybercrime Complaint & Bank Fraud Report

POLICE_COMPLAINT.issue_type: Police Refusal to Register FIR / Formal Written Complaint

evidence_items.name: Evidence of Offence (Photos / Video / Audio / Medical Memo)
evidence_items.why_needed: Substantiates the factual allegations of the cognizable offence.

evidence_items.name: Copy of Original Written Representation / GD Entry
evidence_items.why_needed: Proves the matter was first presented to the local Station House Officer (SHO).

evidence_items.name: Speed Post / Registered Post Delivery Proof to DCP/SP
evidence_items.why_needed: Helps prove when and where an escalation was delivered if a written complaint is sent to the Superintendent of Police.

stages.title: Reported to Local Police Station (SHO)
stages.description: Informal or verbal complaint made at the jurisdictional police station.

stages.title: Formal Written Complaint Submitted under Sec 173(1) BNSS
stages.description: Detailed written complaint presented to SHO with acknowledgment sought.

stages.title: Escalation to Superintendent of Police (SP / DCP)
stages.description: Complaint dispatched via Registered Post to SP / DCP if local police station refuses registration.

stages.title: Consider Magistrate Application under BNSS
stages.description: A Magistrate application may be considered with legal advice after checking the offence, prior representations, evidence, and current procedure.

rights_summary.what_this_means: If the information discloses a cognizable offence, FIR-registration duties may arise under the BNSS and Supreme Court precedent. Classification depends on the facts and should not be guessed.
possible_rights: Right to a free copy of the FIR immediately upon registration under Section 173(2) BNSS.
Right to send written complaint by Registered Post to the Superintendent of Police under Section 173(3) BNSS.
Possible route to approach a Judicial Magistrate under the BNSS after checking procedural requirements with counsel or legal aid.
rights_summary.legal_source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 173) & Lalita Kumari v. Govt of UP (2014 SC).
